newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada nuclear research privatization hits delay.
newsitem.headline: Canada nuclear research privatization hits delay.

text.p: The Canadian government and a consortium led by a unit of British Nuclear Fuels Plc (BNFL) have failed to reach their end-of-June deadline to privatize one of Canada's flagship nuclear research laboratories.

Government talks with Canadian Nuclear Projects Ltd for the company to operate the Whiteshell laboratories in Manitoba were set back by the Canadian federal election earlier in June, spokesmen for the government and company said on Friday.

"From our perspective, it's probably just the election and the (change in) ministers that put a delay in the schedule," David Campbell, spokesman for BNFL's U.S. subsidiary, British Nuclear Fuels Inc, said in a phone interview.
"We want things to get moving," he said. "But we don't see any showstoppers for the moment."
He said no dollar amount had been made public for the deal. The facility is currently run by government agency Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd.
The government hopes to finalize the deal by late summer, a spokeswoman for Natural Resources Minister Anne McLellan said in a phone interview.
"Both parties definitely want to make it happen," she said.
But she said the talks were very complicated and the government had yet to set a new schedule for the talks to conclude.
